Selection-free check of the per-cell null

Source: R/event_fdr.R
null_selection_check.Rd

The null cells of normal mode are selected for having no chromosome / arm call (select_null_cells()), the thresholds are trained on their rows and the budget is verified on the same rows by fold cross-validation, so a selection that truncates the null tail (a too thin parametric null, cells with a noisier than modelled genome) goes unseen. This check splits the autosomes into two halves (odd / even chromosome number), selects the null cells on the rows of one half only, trains the per-cell thresholds as usual on those rows (caller_normal() with the selected cells as null cells and the half as null_chroms: depth t null, rho, fold-cross-validated budget thresholds, the run's calib options), and counts the exceedances (s_comb above its threshold) on the null regions of the OTHER half of the same cells: rows that neither the selection nor the thresholds saw. The two halves are swapped and the counts combined.

Usage

null_selection_check(
  feat,
  params = caller_defaults(),
  multiplets = NULL,
  regions = NULL,
  depth_model = c("t", "gauss"),
  select_args = list(),
  null_chroms = paste0("chr", 1:22),
  false_calls = NULL,
  conf = 0.95
)

Arguments

feat

features long table (as for caller_normal())

params

caller_defaults()

multiplets

cells never selected as null cells

regions

regions table (default regions_from_features())

depth_model

"t" or "gauss"

select_args

extra arguments for select_null_cells() (its chroms is set per half)

null_chroms

the chromosomes whose rows can be null rows in the run; their numbered autosomes are split

false_calls

optional null_false_calls() rates of the run, added as cv_per_1000 (the run's in-sample cross-validated rate on all null rows)

conf

confidence level of the intervals

Value

data.table class, stratum (all = over the strata), n_rows (measured rows), n_exceed, per_1000 (null and real-event exceedances per 1,000 measured rows: an upper bound of the null rate), lo_per_1000, hi_per_1000, nominal_per_1000, insample_rows, insample_exceed, insample_per_1000 (the cross-validated rate on the selection half's null rows of the same passes), cv_per_1000 (with false_calls); attribute halves (half, select_chroms, measure_chroms, n_cells, n_null_cells)

Details

Cells are selected on one half only, so a cell that carries a real event on the measured half stays in and the rows of that event count as exceedances: per_1000 is the null exceedance rate plus the rate of real events on the measured half, an upper bound of the null rate. A rate clearly above the nominal 1 - null_q (and above the in-sample cross-validated rate on the selection half, insample_per_1000) has two possible causes: a selected null that is cleaner than the cells it is applied to (the per-cell false load is then underestimated), or real events in the cells. Read it next to the share of cells with a called event: in a sample without real events the excess measures the selection, in a sample with them it is an upper bound. The halves carry different chromosomes, so a class whose regions differ in their null spread (e.g. chromosomes of very different size) also shows up. Confidence intervals are exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) over rows; rows of one cell overlap (a chromosome and its arms), so they are somewhat too narrow. Costs about one more caller_normal() scoring pass (two half passes without pools). With calib_rho = "chrom" the measured half has no null rows and takes the global rho.
